sections.overview: Gollumjapyx smeagol is a cave-adapted dipluran described in 2006 from the eastern Iberian Peninsula.
sections.identification: It is unpigmented and has elongated appendages and antennae, traits associated with permanent subterranean life.
sections.habitat: It is known from limestone caves and deep subterranean spaces in eastern Spain, including localities in Castellón and Tarragona. The Catalan account reports cave-floor temperatures of 14–17 °C.
sections.diet: It is a predator of small subterranean arthropods; digestive contents included mites and fragments of cave beetles. The Catalan account also characterizes it as a large predator of mites and beetles.
sections.behavior: Its elongated sensory appendages are part of a suite of specializations for darkness, not evidence that it belongs to a different insect order.
sections.reproduction: The original description records cave occurrences but does not establish a reproductive cycle.
sections.ecology: The original taxonomic authors noted that its unusual characters did not establish a clear relationship to other japygid genera. A later comparative account also discusses its pronounced cave-adapted form.
sections.conservation: Catalonia lists it as Vulnerable and identifies cave pollution or alteration and disturbance of surrounding land as threats; this is a regional, not global, assessment.
